claims.head: Like for like: Coyle against Karlsson
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ L2 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) spends at least 50% of its 5-on-5 time against the Golden Knights’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Golden Knights’ second line is Howden, Karlsson and Holtz.
claims.nums: At home: 50% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 27% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Golden Knights’ second line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Columbus home games this season · 6 games, 65 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Columbus’s L2 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) at home: 50% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ second lines. Matchups, Columbus home games this season, 6 games, 65 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face second lines about 27% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

notes.text: Mitch Marner is out and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Alexander Holtz has taken his spot beside William Karlsson and Brett Howden.
Alexander Holtz was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside William Karlsson and Brett Howden.
Ivan Provorov is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Zach Werenski has taken his spot beside Denton Mateychuk.
Damon Severson was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Zach Werenski.

CBJ.head: The Blue Jackets have a hill to climb
CBJ.body: Even though Columbus has home-ice advantage and Vegas will be without Marner, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blue Jackets can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights have a lot going for them
VGK.body: Even though Columbus has home-ice advantage and Vegas will be without Marner, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blue Jackets’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.
